**The grammar, once** — `engine/checks/helpers/provenance.mjs`: the entry grammar (`## <date> · <kind> · <one line>`, the closed kinds, the fields, born first, Mechanism where the kind demands it), the slug marker that ends a rule and names its file, how a pack's carriers are enumerated under either root and which file each names, the audit every check composes, and the two codemods: `markPack` (a proposed marker per unmarked rule and guideline, a `body` per skill from its shape, an empty file per carrier — idempotent, writes no entry) and `convertReferences` (each `references.md` key becomes an entry on the element it named, numeric markers become slugs, a workflow skill's numbers leave the step, the doc goes). The promotion reduction (`reduceText`) is here too.

**The member side** — `engine/migrations/registry.mjs` gains `markProvenance`, a named codemod op like `updateTaskSchedulingFields`, and the record `packs/claudinite-growth/migrations/2026-09-21-provenance-marking/` declares it, so a member's local packs are converted and marked at the converge that delivers this growth version, with no session and nobody remembering. The update flows' io gains `remove` for the doc the conversion retires.

**The growth pack** — `provenance.mjs` (`mark [--dry-run]`, `check`, `convert-references`, `append [--changed]`, `reduce [--public]`, `history`; the append reads one entry from stdin, validates it, and refuses one that reads as a secret through the capture scrub); `provenance-integrity` (world, blocking, `since` 2026-09-20: every carrier names a live file, every file parses; empty files and a pack-root `references.md` are advisory branches, the latter the tolerance #2170 retires) and `provenance-change-recorded` (work, blocking: a carrier whose decision-bearing text changed carries its entry, a file only grows, a deleted carrier's file ends `retired`) replacing `references-integrity`; the `changing-pack-elements` skill forced on every pack file under either root (it held my own edits in this session until loaded, which is the mechanism working); the `backfilling-provenance` skill; `writing-pack-prose`'s references section is now the provenance section; the extraction, dedup, conversion and revalidation skills end with the append, revalidation filling an empty file it meets.

**Curation, preferences, the home** — two rules on the shelf (a README carries use, a carrier change carries its entry) and the descriptive-prose rule's new destination; the promote task carries the reduced file and marks the promoted rule; `generate-project-instructions` mints `_pack.md`; the preferences pack's rule and the advisory `preferences-provenance` check (a preference's file beside the store, existence only); the home's rule on a built design doc moves the owner-decision record onto the element's file.

**The boundaries** — a pack-root `provenance/` never vendors (fixture and real-corpus tests; the real-corpus half asserts absence alone until the marking pass creates the folders, then step 2 adds the non-vacuity guard); the barrier grammar gains the `<folder>/*/<name>` carve-out and the shelf's siblings rule carves `packs/*/provenance` out, so a decision log may name what it explains.

## Decisions taken beyond the design

- **The parser and codemods live in the engine, not the growth pack, and the record is the growth pack's, not the lifecycle pack's.** A migration record's vocabulary is closed to named ops shipped with the engine ("one op with one meaning, not a general escape hatch"), so the member-side marking needs an engine op, and an engine op cannot import a pack. The record sits under the pack whose corpus it marks, as `task-cadence-terms` did. The plan named the lifecycle pack; noted on #2169.
- **Every pack importer of the new helper uses a namespace import with a `typeof` guard** — the `named-import-of-new-engine-export` check's ask, since the two lanes deliver on separate cadences.
- **A marker the line cannot hold within 100 bytes goes on a continuation line of its own**, so the marking pass is one appended line per rule and a re-wrap is nobody's.
- **A marker reads at the end of a rule's lead paragraph, before any nested list**, or at the block's end where a rule was marked after its list.
- **The record's version is `60930.1`, past the landing day on purpose**: the bump task cuts the number after the change lands, so a record cannot know it; a value past the landing day keeps the record in range for the first converge after the pack update reaches a member and drops it out once the pack bumps past it.
- **The rehearsal fixture stays on the retired convention** as the record's own test bed: the converge converts and marks it, and the sweep then reads the marked pack.
- **Two `file-placement` advisories on the helper stand deliberately** (it reaches `engine/pack_loader/` for the skill frontmatter and the folder names): the reach is the cross-cutting concern the fix text names, and the helper sits with the check helpers because the checks and the registry are its consumers.

Both checks carry `since: 2026-09-20`, so the shelf's backlog — 60 skills with no body, 29 rules files with unmarked rules, 22 `references.md` — reads as advisory in the world sweep until step 2 lands; after 2026-10-04 it blocks. Step 2 is the next PR in this stack.

- Hook latency: no hook changed.

description: Running this repo's test suite — the one command that covers it, reading a run's output from a file instead of re-running it, iterating on the tests an edit touches, and staging a new test file before certifying a run. Use before any node --test.
metadata:
-  body: guidelines
force-load-on-tool-calls:
- 'Bash.command /\bnode\s+--test\b/'
script; `ci.yml`'s array is not authoritative. A bash glob without `globstar` is the dangerous
substitute — `packs/*/test/*.test.mjs` reports nothing wrong over 125 of 314 files — while
`node --test <dir>` fails outright and a glob matching nothing exits 1, so only a glob that
-  matches a subset leaves you believing a green run. (whole-suite-command)
+  matches a subset leaves you believing a green run. (4)
- **Read a run's output from a file** — redirect one run and grep that file for the slice you need;
-  never re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice unchanged output. (read-runs-output)
+  never re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice unchanged output. (1)
- **`git add` a new test file before certifying a run green** — `git ls-files` excludes an unstaged
-  file, so the run never executed it; the `untracked-test-file` finding at Stop says which.
-  (git-add-new)
+  file, so the run never executed it; the `untracked-test-file` finding at Stop says which. (2)
- **Iterating on a sweep across many files** — run only the test files the edit touches, plus
`check_the_work`; spend the whole suite and `check_the_world` once, at the end. Both are
-  whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file. (iterating-sweep-across)
+  whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file. (3)
- **Editing a `RULES.md` or `README.md` under `packs/`** — the file that holds a pack's rule index
in step with its prose sits outside the pack, and neither conformance sweep runs it, so add
-  `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` to the files the edit touches. (editing-rules-md)
+  `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` to the files the edit touches. (5)
`Resource: "*"` (scope the *data-plane* grants to your stack instead). `sam deploy` surfaces only
`Waiter ChangeSetCreateComplete failed` — the actual `AccessDenied` is visible only in the
CloudFormation console's **Change sets** tab. Don't paper over it with `AdministratorAccess`.
-  (deploy-role-must)
- **A brand-new AWS account can't create a CloudFront distribution until AWS verifies it.** The
deploy fails
`AccessDenied: Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources` — an
account-level anti-abuse gate, not an IAM or template bug. Open a Support case to get the account
-  verified, and launch against the origin URL directly meanwhile. (brand-new-aws)
+  verified, and launch against the origin URL directly meanwhile.
- **A failed first `CREATE` must be cleaned up before you retry.** A stack left in
`ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` (and a SAM managed-bucket stack stuck in `REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS`) can only be
*deleted*, never updated. And any resource with `DeletionPolicy: Retain` survives the rollback
orphaned, so the retry then fails `already exists` until you delete the orphan too.
-  (failed-first-create)
- **Review the change set before applying — `Replacement: True` on a stateful resource is a
data-loss hard stop.** Replacement creates a *new, empty* resource; a DynamoDB table shows it
whenever an immutable property (its `KeySchema`/`AttributeDefinitions`) changes. Enable stack
**termination protection** too — it's a one-time CLI/API call (`update-termination-protection`),
-  not expressible in the template body. (review-change-set)
+  not expressible in the template body.
- **A custom request header turns even a public GET into a preflighted CORS request.** Any
non-simple header (e.g. a client-version header) makes the browser send an `OPTIONS` preflight, so
the API's CORS `AllowHeaders` must list that header or the real request is blocked *in the
browser* — while server-side unit tests that never run the CORS layer stay green.
-  (custom-request-header)
- **Reach AWS from a session with the AWS CLI or a boto3 script — there is no AWS MCP tool.** A
stack's real state comes from a CLI call (`aws cloudformation describe-stacks …`) — the last
**not pre-installed on the cloud/web runner** (nor `boto3`/`sam`), so declare its install in the
**environment setup script** (`pip install awscli`, or the official bundle) rather than per
session; point it at the sandbox proxy's CA bundle (`AWS_CA_BUNDLE`) if a call fails TLS
-  verification. (reach-aws-session)
+  verification.
+# References — rationale behind this pack's rules and checks
+Maintenance and review material for the `writing-pack-prose` references convention: each entry
+carries the reason a rule or check exists, written so a periodic review can reaffirm — or
+retire — it. Entry keys are file-scoped stable identifiers (gaps allowed, never renumbered): an
+end-of-line `(n)` marker in `RULES.md` cites `RULES-n`, one in a skill cites
+`<skill-name>-n`, and `check:` entries cover checks. No session loads this file for daily work.
+- **(check:aws-sam/handler-path)** Converted from the pack's prose in #136: esbuild's default
+  `outbase` is the entry point's own directory (esbuild's documented behaviour,
+  https://esbuild.github.io/api/#outbase), so SAM's esbuild builder strips a single entry's
+  subdirectory from the artifact and a subdirectory-carrying Handler fails only at first invoke
+  with `Runtime.ImportModuleError`. Reaffirm against esbuild's outbase documentation and SAM's
+  esbuild builder; retire only if either changes that default.
+- **(sam-build-and-deps-1)** Declaring esbuild in `dependencies` does not bloat the deployed artifact: it is
+  not bundled unless the handler imports it, so the usual objection to the remedy — shipping a
+  build tool to production — does not apply. Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467 text (cut
+  by 2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it”, before this
+  pack had a references.md to hold it). Reaffirm against SAM's esbuild builder; retire if it
+  stops running a production-only install.
+- **(sam-template-2)** Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls — a `CachePolicy`
+  defines the cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin — which is
+  why the two are set separately to cache public GETs on one entry while still delivering
+  `Authorization` for authenticated writes. Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467 text (cut by
+  2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it”, before this pack
+  had a references.md to hold it). Reaffirm against CloudFront's managed-policy list; retire if
+  a custom policy is ever allowed to name `Authorization`.
name: sam-build-and-deps

description: Declaring a SAM Lambda's build dependencies — esbuild as a regular dependency for SAM's production-only install, and bundling the AWS SDK packages the handler imports instead of trusting the managed runtime's copy. Use when editing package.json or the build settings of a SAM template.
metadata:
-  body: guidelines
force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
- "package.json"
- "**/template.yaml"
- **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a
*production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and
the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies`, or put it on the
-  runner's `PATH` before `sam build`. (esbuild-must-be)
+  runner's `PATH` before `sam build`. (1)
- **Bundle the AWS SDK into the Lambda artifact rather than relying on the managed runtime's copy.**
The runtime doesn't ship every SDK sub-package (a missing one fails only at invoke), and its
bundled SDK minor version drifts under you. Declare and bundle the SDK packages you import, and
-  pin a non-EOL runtime explicitly rather than letting it float. (bundle-aws-sdk)
+  pin a non-EOL runtime explicitly rather than letting it float.
name: sam-template

description: Shaping a SAM template's CloudFront, API Gateway CORS, cache and DynamoDB index resources — forwarding Authorization, non-http origins, what a CDN hit skips, TTL over invalidation, GSI backfill. Use when editing a SAM template.yaml or template.yml.
metadata:
-  body: guidelines
force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
- "**/template.yaml"
- "**/template.yml"
keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed**
`AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache
policy that omits `Authorization`. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the
-  viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403. (cloudfront-wont-forward)
+  viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403. (2)
- **A CDN cache hit is served before the request reaches the origin or its authorizer**, so you
cannot enforce request auth on a *cacheable* read without edge compute (Lambda@Edge) — and keying
the cache per token destroys the hit rate that justified caching. Treat cacheable endpoints as
public by design, and protect only uncached (write / per-user) paths at the authorizer.
-  (cdn-cache-hit)
- **Prefer a short CloudFront TTL over per-write cache invalidation.** Invalidation is billed per
path beyond a small monthly free allowance, so a write-through design that invalidates on every
write is a cost trap; a short TTL plus optimistic local rendering hides the propagation delay from
-  the writer. (prefer-short-cloudfront)
+  the writer.
## API Gateway CORS
- **API Gateway HTTP API (v2) rejects a `chrome-extension://` origin in CORS `AllowOrigins`** with
`BadRequestException: Invalid format for origin`, accepting only `http(s)://…` or `*`. An API
fronted by a browser-extension (or other non-`http`) origin must therefore set `AllowOrigins:
-  ['*']` and rely on its **JWT authorizer**, not CORS, as the security boundary. (api-gateway-http)
+  ['*']` and rely on its **JWT authorizer**, not CORS, as the security boundary.
## DynamoDB
- **Adding a DynamoDB GSI does not backfill existing items.** The `UpdateTable` is additive and
indexes only items that already carry the index's key attributes; rows written earlier stay
invisible until each is rewritten with those attributes. Plan an explicit backfill pass if
-  pre-existing data must appear in the new index. (adding-dynamodb-gsi)
+  pre-existing data must appear in the new index.

- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own — research it against the vendor's live documentation, capture what is portable as a technology skill with declared checks, and wire the project's use of it as a task in its structural local pack. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- revalidating-rules: Re-probe the pack rules whose truth lives outside the repository — harness tool contracts, token reach, whether an MCP tool exists, a platform's behaviour — and correct the ones that have gone stale. Use when a revalidation sweep runs over a corpus of packs, or when asked whether a rule's environmental claim still holds.
- running-the-suite: Running this repo's test suite — the one command that covers it, reading a run's output from a file instead of re-running it, iterating on the tests an edit touches, and staging a new test file before certifying a run. Use before any node --test.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, get the owner's approval of the plan itself — a line per step, the dependency graph, each link's automerge policy — before filing any of its issues, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, size the links (how many PRs, what each one's diff is predicted to touch and the automerge policy that prediction becomes) and write the chain to survive a policy park, a red CI or a PR closed unmerged, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written — RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon — brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, the marker that names a rule's provenance file. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a check that scans the repo picks its file set, strips comments before matching a forbidden token, and proves itself silent against real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own — research it against the vendor's live documentation, capture what is portable as a technology skill with declared checks, and wire the project's use of it as a task in its structural local pack. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.

- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.

- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. attachment.content:
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own — research it against the vendor's live documentation, capture what is portable as a technology skill with declared checks, and wire the project's use of it as a task in its structural local pack. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- revalidating-rules: Re-probe the pack rules whose truth lives outside the repository — harness tool contracts, token reach, whether an MCP tool exists, a platform's behaviour — and correct the ones that have gone stale. Use when a revalidation sweep runs over a corpus of packs, or when asked whether a rule's environmental claim still holds.
- running-the-suite: Running this repo's test suite — the one command that covers it, reading a run's output from a file instead of re-running it, iterating on the tests an edit touches, and staging a new test file before certifying a run. Use before any node --test.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, get the owner's approval of the plan itself — a line per step, the dependency graph, each link's automerge policy — before filing any of its issues, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, size the links (how many PRs, what each one's diff is predicted to touch and the automerge policy that prediction becomes) and write the chain to survive a policy park, a red CI or a PR closed unmerged, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written — RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon — brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, the marker that names a rule's provenance file. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a check that scans the repo picks its file set, strips comments before matching a forbidden token, and proves itself silent against real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

8	// THE WORK HALF of the provenance convention (the provenance design, #2136): a change
9	// that alters a carrier's decision-bearing text carries the entry that records the
10	// decision, on the file the carrier names, in the same change. The skill says append;
11	// this says it again at the Stop hook when the session did not.
12	//
13	// What counts as a change an entry is owed for: a rule or guideline whose normalized
14	// text differs from the base's (markers and whitespace off — the marking pass owes
15	// nothing), a skill whose description, load triggers or body text moved, a check
16	// module or declaration whose non-comment content moved, a task's declaration or
17	// worker, the manifest. A carrier with no file at all is the world half's finding, not
18	// this one's.
19	//
20	// A provenance file only grows: a changed file keeps every base line in place and adds
21	// after the last entry. A carrier this change deleted named a file whose last entry
22	// must now be `retired` — asserted from the tree's side, since a removed-lines check
23	// cannot see a deleted file.
24	const rule = {
25	  id: 'provenance-change-recorded',
26	  severity: 'blocking',
27	  scope: 'work',
28	  since: '2026-09-20',
29	  doc: 'packs/claudinite-growth/skills/changing-pack-elements/SKILL.md',
30	  description: 'A change to a pack carrier lands with an entry on its provenance file, and a provenance file only grows',
31	  why: 'the decision behind a change exists only in the head of whoever made it, at the moment they made it; a log appended later is a reconstruction',
32	
33	  run(work) {
34	    if (typeof provenance.packCarriers !== 'function') return []; // an engine that predates the helper
35	    const { packCarriers, provenanceFiles, packDirsIn, fileOfId, elementIdOf, PROVENANCE_DIR, PACK_ELEMENT } = provenance;
36	    if (work.onDefaultBranch()) return [];
37	    const changed = work.changedFiles.map((f) => f.replace(/\\/g, '/'));
38	    const deleted = (work.deleted ?? []).map((f) => f.replace(/\\/g, '/'));
39	    const packs = packDirsIn([...changed, ...deleted]);
40	    if (!packs.length) return [];
41	    // The head tree is everything tracked plus the run's untracked files — never the
42	    // changed set alone, which would read every untouched carrier as deleted.
43	    const headFiles = [...work.tracked, ...work.untracked];
44	    const head = { exists: (p) => work.exists(p), read: (p) => work.read(p), listDir: (p) => listFrom(headFiles, p) };
45	    const baseFiles = [...new Set([...work.tracked, ...deleted])].filter((p) => work.readBase(p) !== null);
46	    const base = { exists: (p) => work.readBase(p) !== null, read: (p) => work.readBase(p), listDir: (p) => listFrom(baseFiles, p) };
47	    const out = [];
48	    const touched = (p) => changed.includes(p);
49	
50	    for (const dir of packs) {
51	      const now = packCarriers(dir, head);
52	      const before = packCarriers(dir, base);
53	      const filesNow = provenanceFiles(dir, head);
54	      const filesBefore = provenanceFiles(dir, base);
55	      // A pack with no provenance folder at the base is being brought onto the
56	      // convention by this change — the marking pass, or a member's first converge
57	      // onto it — and its elements' history is the backfill's, not this change's.
58	      if (!filesBefore.size) continue;
59	      const gained = (id) => {
60	        const h = filesNow.get(id);
61	        if (!h) return false;
62	        const b = filesBefore.get(id);
63	        return h.entries.length > (b?.entries.length ?? 0);
64	      };
65	      const owes = (id, file, line, what) => {
66	        if (!filesNow.has(id) || gained(id)) return;
67	        out.push(finding(rule, {
68	          file, line,
69	          what: `${what}, and ${dir}/${PROVENANCE_DIR}/${fileOfId(id)} gained no entry in this change`,
70	          fix: `append the entry that records the decision — its kind (reworded, strengthened, weakened, moved, converted, trigger-changed, policy-changed, severity-changed, split, merged) and why — through \`node <path to claudinite-growth>/provenance.mjs append ${dir.slice(dir.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)} ${id}\`, reading the entry from stdin`,
71	        }));
72	      };
73	
74	      // Rules and guidelines: by trigger, text compared marker-free.
75	      const wasByTrigger = new Map([...before.rules, ...before.guidelines].map((r) => [r.trigger, r]));
76	      for (const r of [...now.rules, ...now.guidelines]) {
77	        if (!r.slug || !touched(r.file)) continue;
78	        const was = wasByTrigger.get(r.trigger);
79	        if (!was) owes(r.slug, r.file, r.line, `"${r.trigger}" is new`);
80	        else if (was.text !== r.text) owes(r.slug, r.file, r.line, `"${r.trigger}" reads differently from the base`);
81	      }
82	      // Skills: the file changed beyond whitespace.
83	      for (const s of now.skills) {
84	        if (!s.present || !touched(s.file)) continue;
85	        const b = base.read(s.file);
86	        if (b !== null && normalize(b) === normalize(head.read(s.file))) continue;
87	        if (b !== null && skillOnlyMarkedOrBodied(b, head.read(s.file))) continue;
88	        owes(s.name, s.file, null, `skill ${s.name} changed`);
89	      }
90	      // Checks, tasks, the manifest: non-comment content moved.
91	      const seenCheck = new Set();
92	      for (const c of now.checks) {
93	        const id = elementIdOf(c.id);
94	        if (seenCheck.has(id) || !touched(c.file)) continue;
95	        seenCheck.add(id);
96	        const b = base.read(c.file);
97	        if (b !== null && c.file.endsWith('.mjs') && commentOnly(c.file, b, head.read(c.file))) continue;
98	        if (b !== null && c.file.endsWith('.json') && !declarationChanged(b, head.read(c.file), c.id)) continue;
99	        owes(id, c.file, null, `check ${c.id} changed`);
100	      }
101	      for (const t of now.tasks) {
102	        const files = changed.filter((f) => f.startsWith(`${t.dir}/`));
103	        if (!files.length) continue;
104	        if (files.every((f) => f.endsWith('.mjs') && base.read(f) !== null && commentOnly(f, base.read(f), head.read(f)))) continue;
105	        owes(t.id, files[0], null, `task ${t.id} changed`);
106	      }
107	      if (now.manifest && touched(`${dir}/pack.mjs`)) {
108	        const b = base.read(`${dir}/pack.mjs`);
109	        if (!(b !== null && commentOnly(`${dir}/pack.mjs`, b, head.read(`${dir}/pack.mjs`)))) owes(PACK_ELEMENT, `${dir}/pack.mjs`, null, 'the manifest changed');
110	      }
111	
112	      // A provenance file only grows.
113	      for (const [id, h] of filesNow) {
114	        if (!touched(h.file)) continue;
115	        const b = filesBefore.get(id);
116	        if (!b || b.text.trim() === '') continue;
117	        if (!h.text.startsWith(b.text.replace(/\s+$/, ''))) {
118	          out.push(finding(rule, {
119	            file: h.file,
120	            what: `${fileOfId(id)} lost or altered a line it had at the base — a provenance file only grows`,
121	            fix: 'restore the file to its base text and append what this change decides after the last entry; a wrong entry is corrected by a later entry, never edited',
122	          }));
123	        }
124	      }
125	
126	      // A deleted carrier's file ends with retired.
127	      const gone = [];
128	      const nowTriggers = new Set([...now.rules, ...now.guidelines].map((r) => r.trigger));
129	      for (const r of [...before.rules, ...before.guidelines]) if (r.slug && !nowTriggers.has(r.trigger)) gone.push({ id: r.slug, what: `rule "${r.trigger}"` });
130	      const nowSkills = new Set(now.skills.filter((s) => s.present).map((s) => s.name));
131	      for (const s of before.skills) if (s.present && !nowSkills.has(s.name)) gone.push({ id: s.name, what: `skill ${s.name}` });
132	      const nowChecks = new Set(now.checks.map((c) => c.id));
133	      for (const c of before.checks) if (!nowChecks.has(c.id)) gone.push({ id: elementIdOf(c.id), what: `check ${c.id}` });
134	      const nowTasks = new Set(now.tasks.map((t) => t.id));
135	      for (const t of before.tasks) if (!nowTasks.has(t.id)) gone.push({ id: t.id, what: `task ${t.id}` });
136	      for (const g of gone) {
137	        const f = filesNow.get(g.id);
138	        const retiredNow = f && f.entries.length && f.entries[f.entries.length - 1].kind === 'retired' && (filesBefore.get(g.id)?.status !== 'retired');
139	        if (retiredNow) continue;
140	        out.push(finding(rule, {
141	          file: `${dir}/${PROVENANCE_DIR}/${fileOfId(g.id)}`,
142	          what: `${g.what} is gone from ${dir} in this change, and its file's last entry is not retired`,
143	          fix: `append \`## <date> · retired · <why>\` to ${fileOfId(g.id)} in the same change — the decision to remove is a decision, and the file stays`,
144	        }));
145	      }
146	    }
147	    return out;
148	  },
149	};
150	
151	const normalize = (t) => String(t ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
152	
153	// The marking pass's own edits to a skill: a `body:` line and markers on guideline
154	// bullets. Neither is a decision, so a skill that changed only so owes nothing.
155	function skillOnlyMarkedOrBodied(before, after) {
156	  const strip = (t) => normalize(String(t)
157	    .replace(/^\s*body:\s*(workflow|guidelines)\s*$/gm, '')
158	    .replace(/^metadata:\s*$/gm, '') // the block `mark` opens to hold the body
159	    .replace(/\s*\([a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+\)\s*$/gm, '')
160	    .replace(/\s*\(\d+(?:\s*,\s*\d+)*\)\s*$/gm, ''));
161	  return strip(before) === strip(after);
162	}
163	
164	// One declaration in a declared-checks.json moved: compared parsed, by id.
165	function declarationChanged(before, after, id) {
166	  const find = (t) => { try { return JSON.stringify((JSON.parse(t) ?? []).find((d) => d?.id === id) ?? null); } catch { return null; } };
167	  return find(before) !== find(after);
168	}
169	
170	function listFrom(files, p) {
171	  const names = new Set();
172	  const prefix = `${p}/`;
173	  for (const f of files) {
174	    const n = f.replace(/\\/g, '/');
175	    if (n.startsWith(prefix)) names.add(n.slice(prefix.length).split('/')[0]);
176	  }
177	  return names.size ? [...names] : null;
178	}
179	
180	export default rule;
181	
</system-reminder>
